questions.question: What did Grad B say about the structure of the belief net?
questions.reference_answer: It is necessary for the belief-net to have at least one layer of nodes between the features and the final output. This makes the structure more flexible in terms of coding feature-layer probabilities.

oracle.answer: Grad B mentioned that setting up all the probabilities for the belief net would be a hassle and that moving to the next step of learning would handicap them since they don't know belief nets very well. They also suggested adding a middle layer to the belief net to represent hidden variables such as whether someone is a tourist, running an errand, or in a hurry, which could affect their behavior and choices.

questions.question: How would the middle layer work?
questions.reference_answer: The values these nodes take feed into the middle layer nodes identified as hidden variables of the user/device interaction, such as whether the user is on tour, running an errand or in a hurry. These, in turn, help infer whether the user wants to see, enter or simply approach a building.

oracle.answer: The middle layer would work by identifying hidden variables such as whether someone is on a tour, running an errand, or in a hurry, based on their communicated abstract ideas and previous statements. These hidden variables help determine the context of their travel intentions, influencing how they utilize the features related to their destination and mode of transportation.

questions.question: What was the importance of SmartKom?
questions.reference_answer: SmartKom, although it does not code for intentions as specified in this task, provides a model of the discourse, which can be useful for the detection of features through querying and anaphora resolution.

oracle.answer: The importance of SmartKom lies in its role as a comprehensive discourse processing system. It includes an elaborate module that serves as the memory of the entire system, tracking who said what and maintaining the context necessary for anaphora resolution and filling in omitted structures. This allows SmartKom to manage the flow of information throughout a conversation, ensuring that previous information is retained and utilized appropriately, even when not explicitly referenced through anaphora. Additionally, SmartKom assists in coordinating gesture and screen interactions, storing what was presented on the screen at specific locations.
